note: Adapted from the original description by Wasmann (1897b), written in German (the alate also has a Latin diagnosis); covers all three castes, soldier, worker and alate. Some figures and words in the scan are damaged (for example the ratio of antenna to head length); only the legible values are recorded.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body slender cylindrical, constricted at the thorax, body length 6—7 mm, of which the head with mandibles is 3 mm; mandibles nearly 1 mm long, head width 0.8 mm. Body yellowish white, head yellowish brown with the front dark brown, mandibles black. Head more than twice as long as wide, narrowly cylindrical, slightly flattened dorsally, almost as high as wide, strongly shining, the anterior part of the frons dull. At the anterior quarter of the head length there is a depressed fontanelle, from which two forked longitudinal grooves run, gradually deepening, to the two corners of the anterior margin of the frons, ending above the base of the mandibles; the frontal area between the two grooves is not raised. Clypeus weakly raised like a pad, with one longitudinal groove. Labrum twice as wide as long, sides straight, anterior margin rounded and slightly wavy where it meets the sides. Mandibles slightly shorter than half the head length, narrow, slightly knife-curved, inner margin with many fine teeth, of which two on the left mandible are somewhat larger. Antennae 13-segmented, about three quarters of the head length, not thickened towards the apex, brown, each segment with a white ring at its base; basal segment elongate cylindrical, thicker than segments 1 and 3; segment 2 elongate cylindrical, much longer than the very short segment 3; segments 4—13 as thick as the basal segment, segments 4—8 only slightly longer than wide, the following ones slightly conical except the oval last segment. Pronotum only half as wide as the head, with a distinct transverse groove; anterior lobe narrow, strongly upturned, rounded, deeply and narrowly incised in the middle; anterior margin of the pronotum wavy on both sides of the anterior lobe; posterior part of the pronotum raised like a ridge, with a longitudinal groove, dropping steeply backwards and strongly narrowed behind the lateral angles, so that the pronotum seen from above is broadly cordate or broadly triangular. Mesonotum as wide as the pronotum, half as long, posterior margin raised in a semicircular arch; metanotum slightly wider and slightly longer than the mesonotum, its posterior margin only weakly raised in a semi-annular arch. Legs rather short, no pulvillus between the claws.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Body length 4—5 mm, yellowish white; head rounded oval, pale leather yellow, mostly with a very distinct coronal suture extending across the occiput.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Small, pitch black, clothed with yellowish brown hairs; antennae brown with white rings; clypeus, mouthparts, ventral surface of the body and legs yellowish brown; head nearly 1/2 wider than the thorax, oval. Ocelli small, far from the compound eye; frontal ocellus absent. Antennae as long as the head, 14-segmented, segment 3 the smallest. Pronotum semicircular, deeply notched in the middle of the posterior margin. Wings greyish brown, costa brown. Measurements: body length 4.5—5 mm, wing length 7 mm. Related to Microcerotermes sikorae, chiefly distinguished by the deeply notched posterior margin of the pronotum; somewhat smaller and slightly darker; clypeus a sharply delimited yellowish brown; frons weakly concave and without a raised dot, whereas in sikorae the frons is not concave and has a distinctly raised dot at the site of the missing frontal ocellus; wing venation almost the same as in sikorae; antennae also 14-segmented with a very small segment 3, but stouter and more strongly thickened towards the apex, the antepenultimate segment still spherical (not longer than wide), whereas in sikorae it is clearly longer than wide.
